answer: Robotic agents operating across an orchard prevent Sybil attacks using physical substrate compliance proofs. To authenticate, each node depresses an actuated quill into tree branches, recording the localized viscoelastic response curve. Because proofs require physical contact, an attacker must purchase dedicated actuation hardware and expend battery power for each identity. During a gale, however, violent wind gusts distort the force curves, causing honest agents to fail validation.
